research_question: How many Denisovan admixture pulses; do components differ across populations
populations: European, East Asian, South Asian, admixed American (PUR/CLM/MXL/PEL), SGDP Papuan
method: Reference-free Sprime (S*-like) introgressed-segment detection; match-rate of segments to Altai Neanderthal & Altai Denisovan; two-component Gaussian mixture test
main_finding: Two Denisovan components: high-altair-affinity (mu~0.82-0.86, ~1/3 of East Asian Denisovan segments) and moderate-affinity (mu~0.46-0.52, dominant in Papuans/South Asians). Two-component test significant ONLY in CHS/CHB/CDX/JPT (+FIN/Punjabi), NOT in American pops
limitations: Americans in Fig4 are ADMIXED 1000G pops; authors explicitly say American lower match rates are 'likely due to admixture/LD causing false positives'; no tract dates; single Denisovan reference
relevance_to_current_project: CENTRAL. Establishes the two-component framework but does NOT show Native Americans carry a Papuan-like component; authors attribute American Denisovan segments to 'Native American ancestors related to East Asians'. Fig4 row 4 (American + SGDP Papuan) is the source of the hypothesis but does not justify it

research_question: Geographic extent of Denisovan ancestry; relationship between EE/NA and Oceanian Denisovan ancestry
data_type: Genome-wide SNP data, 2493 individuals from 221 populations
populations: Eastern Eurasian, Native American (EE/NA), Oceanian (Papuan, Australian)
method: Correlation of Denisovan-ancestry estimate with New Guinea vs Australian ancestry components
main_finding: Widespread VERY LOW LEVEL Denisovan ancestry across EE/NA; in Oceania correlated with New Guinea (not Australian) ancestry (recent gene flow); in EE/NA EQUALLY correlated with New Guinea AND Australian ancestry, suggesting a common source for EE/NA and Oceanian Denisovan ancestry
limitations: SNP data (not WGS); correlation-based (not a formal D-stat/tract test); cannot distinguish 'common ancestry with' from 'gene flow from' common ancestor of New Guineans + Australians
relevance_to_current_project: VERY HIGH. Already found the low-level EE/NA Denisovan signal and its equal Papuan/Australian correlation -- this IS the hypothesis. Provides the population-level motivation; project must test it with controlled D-stats + diagnostic markers on AADR ancients
reproducible_with_aadr: Partially (SNP-based D-stats reproducible; their correlation design needs modern reference panels present in AADR HO)
notes: VERIFIED by fetching PubMed PMID 26104010 this session

research_question: How many divergent Denisovan ancestries in Papuans; their relationships
method: IBDmix reference-based tract detection + joint demographic modeling; two-ancestry vs single-ancestry model comparison
main_finding: At least two (likely three) deeply divergent Denisovan ancestries in Papuans; distinct components introgressed at different times; one component closer to Altai Denisovan than the other
limitations: Model-dependent; Papuan-specific; requires WGS + phasing; IBDmix needs an archaic reference
relevance_to_current_project: HIGH. Defines the 'multiple divergent Denisovan lineages' framework that the project's Tier-5 (Papuan-like vs Han-like split) must reference; supports Model 4 (structured Denisovan source)
notes: VERIFIED citation by fetching DOI 10.1016/j.cell.2019.02.035 this session
